key_insight: A physics-informed multihead neural network can learn a low-dimensional latent manifold that captures families of PDE solutions beyond the initial condition itself.
engineering_relevance: This offers a compact, reproducible way to build reduced-order surrogates for simulating parametric PDE dynamics and analyzing dominant modes of variation.
method: Shared-body multihead PINN learns a latent embedding while linear heads reconstruct solutions for different initial conditions.
A head-orthogonalization penalty removes degeneracies and stabilizes principal components across training runs.
Frequency content is summarized by Fourier-shell contributions to each principal component, yielding an invariant spectral profile.
evidence_signal: On the 1D viscous Burgers equation, a latent dimension of 20 compresses the learned manifold so that only 2–4 PCs explain about 95% and 4–7 PCs explain about 99% of latent variance, with similar behavior for heat and wave equations.
watch_item: Because the initial condition is built into the output by construction, the learned components describe extra variability rather than the full solution, so interpretations should be made in that reduced residual space.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Neural Embeddings of PDE Solution Families
